name: Inhibition_Floor
description: Combined inhibitors cannot reduce non-haem absorption below 6% of the base value (a 94% reduction).
rationale: Strongest single-meal inhibition in our evidence (black tea, Hurrell 1999). Stops multiplied factors going beyond anything measured.

name: Phytate_P_Fraction
description: Phytate phosphorus = 28.2% of phytic acid mass.
rationale: Stoichiometry: 6 P atoms (6 x 30.97) in phytic acid (660.04 g/mol). Converts PhyFoodComp phytate mg to the phytate P doses used by Hallberg 1989.

name: Absorbed_Iron_Reference
description: Absorbed-iron reference = UK RNI x EFSA total dietary absorption (16% men, 18% women 19-50, 16% women 50+).
rationale: UK figures are intakes; EFSA baselines convert them to absorbed iron. Women 50+ use the men's 16% (no longer menstruating). Superseded by ASSUME_015 and ASSUME_016 (2026-11-08): engine totals are not comparable with EFSA's whole-diet figures.

name: Default_Meal_Window
description: Drinks and calcium within 60 minutes after the meal count towards it, unless a rule gives its own window.
rationale: Ahmad Fuzi 2017 showed tea's effect was reduced (not removed) at 60 minutes. Coffee has its own 120-minute window (Morck 1983).

name: Ascorbic_Acid_Phytate_Scaling
description: Proportion of phytate inhibition removed = min(1, vitamin C mg / (30 x max(1, phytate P mg / 58))).
rationale: Siegenberg 1991: 30 mg ascorbic acid overcame inhibition from up to 58 mg phytate P. Linear scaling outside that is an assumption.

name: Calcium_Below_165mg
description: Calcium effect rises linearly from 0% at 0 mg to the 165 mg range; 165-600 mg uses the 50-60% range; held above 600 mg.
rationale: Hallberg 1991 reports dose-related inhibition from 40 mg; the abstract gives figures only at 165 mg and 300-600 mg.

name: Polyphenol_Band_Interpolation
description: Below 20 mg: linear from 0%. 20-50 mg: 50-70%. 50-100 mg: linear between bands. 100-400 mg: 60-90%. Above 400 mg: held.
rationale: Hurrell 1999 reports only the two dose bands.

name: Haem_Fraction_Of_MFP_Iron
description: 40% of the iron in meat, fish and poultry is haem iron.

name: Drinks_Before_Meal
description: Drinks more than 60 minutes before the meal have no effect; drinks 0-60 minutes before count as with the meal.
rationale: Morck 1983: coffee 1 h before a meal had no effect. Extended to other drinks.

name: Missing_Inhibitor_Data
description: Foods with no phytate or polyphenol data count as 0 and raise a data-gap flag.
rationale: Avoids inventing values; the UI and alerts say the estimate may be high.

name: Food_Polyphenols_Not_Modelled
description: Polyphenol modifiers apply to drinks only in v1.
rationale: Hurrell 1999 dose bands were measured with drinks. Applying them to food polyphenols is an untested extrapolation.

name: Vitamin_C_Spent_On_Phytate
description: Vitamin C used to counteract phytate (up to 30 mg per 58 mg phytate P) does not also count as a Monsen enhancer.
rationale: Siegenberg 1991: 30 mg ascorbic acid with phytate gave the same absorption as the plain meal, not more. Avoids counting vitamin C twice.

name: Phytate_From_PhyFoodComp
description: Food phytate = median of matching PhyFoodComp 1.0 rows, each scaled to the CoFID food's dry matter; composite foods use an estimated share of dry matter (dm_share).
rationale: PhyFoodComp values vary widely by country, variety and method; the median of dry-matter-scaled rows is robust to outliers. Rules are in data/curated/phytate_mapping.csv; every row used is listed in data/processed/phytate_audit.csv.

name: Serving_Sizes
description: Serving sizes in curated_foods.csv are typical UK portions, not measured.
rationale: Users adjust portions on the confirm screen.

name: Engine_Consistent_Daily_Target
description: Absorbed-iron target = UK RNI x the engine's fractional absorption of a balanced reference day (data/curated/reference_day.csv).
rationale: The engine multiplies single-meal inhibitor effects measured with simple bread meals, so its daily totals run well below whole-diet estimates (EFSA 16-18%; Monsen and Hallberg-Hulthen about 12% on real diets, PMC5986529). Scoring a reference day with the same engine keeps the target on the same scale: eating like the reference day meets the target.

name: Inhibitor_Free_Potential
description: A meal's potential = haem iron x 25% + non-haem iron x Monsen base with all its vitamin C and meat, and no inhibitors. Share of potential = absorbed / potential.
rationale: A relative measure that does not depend on absolute calibration; shows how much the meal's inhibitors cost.
